transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. I'm here because... well, things have been pretty rough lately. Ever since they made me the acting workflow lead at my job, I've just been walking into the warehouse already tense. 

I'm snapping at people over little SAP errors, and I'm missing cycle-count deadlines that I never, ever used to miss. It's just really taking it out of me. By the time I get home, I'm completely drained. I don't even have the energy to play basketball or work on my sketches anymore. I just can't seem to get a handle on it.
When you're away from work, do you still feel this tense and drained?

Yeah, I really do. It feels like work is just taking over my entire life right now. Like I said, I've completely stopped showing up for basketball, and I don't even use my usual sketching time anymore because I'm just too exhausted when I get home. 

And it's not just affecting my off hours, either. It's getting to the point where my supervisor actually had to bring up those missed cycle-count deadlines during a recent performance check-in. So yeah, I just can't seem to shake it off, even when I leave the warehouse.
If you were no longer in this acting workflow lead role, do you think these problems would mostly go away?

Yeah, I really think they would. But... well, I'm still doing the acting lead job right now. I'm dealing with those extra responsibilities every single day. Since they haven't taken me out of the role, the situation hasn't ended yet for me to actually see things go back to normal. I'm just still right in the middle of it.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
Not really down or depressed, no. Just... stressed, I guess. Overwhelmed by all of it. I don't feel sad or hopeless, just completely burnt out from the pressure at work.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about things other than this work role?
No, not really. It's pretty much just the work stuff. I mean, regular day-to-day things don't bother me that much. It's really just the pressure from this lead position that's constantly on my mind.
Since this role change started, have you been feeling anxious?

I don't think I'd call it anxious, no. I mean, I'm definitely stressed out about all the extra work, like I said, but I'm not sitting around feeling nervous or panicky. It's really just the heavy pressure of trying to keep up with everything they've piled on me.
Since this started, have you lost interest or enjoyment in the things you usually like to do?

Yeah, I have. I've stopped showing up for my regular basketball games, and I haven't been doing my usual sketching time either. It just feels like work is taking over my entire life right now. 

And it's not even like I'm keeping up at work, either... my supervisor actually had to bring up some missed cycle-count deadlines during a recent performance check-in. So, yeah, I'm just not doing the things I usually like because I'm so bogged down by all this.
Has this work stress noticeably hurt your performance on the job?

Yeah, like I was just mentioning, it definitely has. That's what I meant about my supervisor bringing up those missed cycle-count deadlines during my performance check-in. I'm just falling behind. And it's bleeding into everything else, too—like I said, I've completely stopped going to basketball and doing my sketching because it just feels like work is taking over my entire life right now.
Do you feel your reaction to this work role has been stronger than most people would have in the same situation?

I'm not really sure about that. I mean... they dumped a whole lot of extra responsibilities on me all at once. I feel like anyone would be pretty stressed out and overwhelmed by it. So, I don't know if my reaction is worse than most people's... I just know it's a lot to handle right now.
When you think about work, do you feel anxious?

Yeah, I definitely do. Ever since they made me the acting workflow lead, the stress is just... constant. I walk into the warehouse and I'm already tense before my shift even starts. I've even been snapping over little SAP errors, which really isn't like me. 

The whole thing just leaves me completely drained. Like I was saying earlier, that's why I'm missing those cycle-count deadlines I never used to miss, and going home way too exhausted for basketball or my sketches. But yeah, that feeling of being tense and on edge about work is definitely there every day.
Compared with what most people would feel in the same acting lead role, do you think your reaction has been stronger than usual?

I... I think you just asked me that, didn't you? Like I said, I really don't know if it's stronger than usual. They threw a massive amount of extra work at me without much warning. I feel like most people would be pretty overwhelmed by it. So, no, I don't necessarily think my reaction is worse than anyone else's would be.
